clue.text: Saucier boss is heartless

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the five-letter word for boss goes

parts.note: a chief is the boss or head of an organisation

explanation.surface: A sauce cook grumbles that the head of the kitchen has no compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle letter I from CHIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucier is the specialist cook in a kitchen brigade who makes the sauces, so is one kind of kitchen professional.

clue.text: Martyr capturing hearts is a hero

indicators.note: capturing means the martyr's name holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Edmund Campion was a Jesuit priest martyred under Elizabeth I
H is the abbreviation for the card suit hearts

explanation.surface: A martyr who wins people's hearts is hailed as a hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is someone who fights for a cause, a victor or hero figure.

clue.text: Damn heap at bottom of river

indicators.note: in a down clue, being at the bottom of something means coming below it in the grid

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a heap or crate is slang for an old, battered car

explanation.surface: Someone curses a wreck of a car dumped on a riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or denounce, the verb sense of damn.

clue.text: A feature of Hong Kong ——— junk entering island by river?

indicators.note: entering means the junk goes inside the island's name

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides
junk, as rubbish, is scrap

explanation.surface: Hong Kong's harbour suggests a Chinese junk sailing up to an island by a river mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junk' pretends to be the Chinese sailing boat famous in Hong Kong harbour, but it means rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hong Kong is famous for its dense forest of very tall buildings, so a tower block is one of its features.

clue.text: County girl and son missing on rocky island

indicators.note: missing says the son is absent, so that letter comes out

parts.note: a skerry is a small rocky island or reef, especially off Scotland
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A girl from a county loses her son while out on a rocky island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl' is a second hint: Kerry is also a girl's name. Kerry is a county in the south-west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerry is one of the Irish counties, in Munster, so an example of a county.

clue.text: One leisurewear item in a couple of cases

parts.note: two kinds of case: a shell is an outer case, and a suit is a case in a law court
two kinds of case: a shell is an outer case, and a suit is a case in a law court

explanation.surface: A single tracksuit-style garment ends up packed in two suitcases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like luggage but gives two different senses: a protective casing and a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell suit is a shiny nylon tracksuit popular as casual wear in the 1980s and 90s.

clue.text: Possibly a carer's turn at moving dining area

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be one possible arrangement of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Perhaps it is a carer's turn to help at shifting the dining room furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges A CARERS TURN AT. 'moving' looks like the anagram signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A train carriage where meals are served is a dining area that travels along with the train.

clue.text: Baked dish without salt upset Murphy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the pie goes around the sailor

parts.note: a pie is a baked dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the sailor's word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a salt or tar is an old sailor

explanation.surface: Someone called Murphy is upset that a baked dish was made with no salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking; RAT is TAR upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy is a slang word for a potato, from the Irish surname, and pratie is the Irish dialect word for a potato.

clue.text: Poet's unfinished paean divides monarchs

indicators.note: divides means the shortened song splits the monarchs apart

parts.note: two monarchs: R for rex, king, and ER for Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: unfinished means the song loses its last letter

parts.note: a paean is a song of praise, a hymn

explanation.surface: A poet's half-written song of praise causes a rift between kings and queens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monarchs' gives two royal ciphers, rex and Elizabeth Regina, and 'divides' means the shortened song sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymer is someone who writes verse, often a lesser poet or versifier.

clue.text: He helps criminal answer more sensibly

parts.note: doing better means doing something more wisely or sensibly

explanation.surface: A criminal's helper is told to answer the police more sensibly.
explanation.definitionFit: An abettor is an accomplice who encourages or assists someone committing a crime.

clue.text: What women may put on to study men? Rubbish!

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, not officers
pants is British slang for rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that women dress up in order to study men.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTS as an exclamation is British slang for 'rubbish!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Toreador pants are tight calf-length trousers worn by women, so something they may put on.

clue.text: Caught, by the way, in possession of soft drug

indicators.note: the easy piece takes possession of the others, holding them inside

parts.note: something soft is easy or undemanding
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ST, street, is a way or road

explanation.surface: Someone is arrested and, incidentally, found carrying a soft drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft drug' reads as one phrase, but 'soft' gives EASY, which holds C and ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is the street name of the illegal stimulant MDMA, a recreational drug.

clue.text: Drink given to small boys drawing

parts.note: port is a fortified wine, a drink
two boys' names in short form: Ray and Al
two boys' names in short form: Ray and Al

explanation.surface: Little boys are handed a fortified wine, which seems unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small boys' gives two short names, not children.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a depiction of someone, and a drawing is one such depiction.

clue.text: I left in time being alert

indicators.note: in says the first person and the side letter sit inside the period of time

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone says they left early, being alert to how late it was.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means quick and nimble, whether in body or mind, so mentally alert.

clue.text: Run rings round old-fashioned guy at work

parts.note: out of fashion or simply out means old-fashioned
a guy is a man
an oeuvre is a work, or an artist's body of work

explanation.surface: An unfashionable chap at his job is easily beaten by others.
explanation.definitionFit: To run rings round someone is to outwit or outdo them easily, the same idea as outsmart.

clue.text: Choirmaster (not married one) composed for many players

indicators.note: composed suggests the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A choirmaster who is unmarried writes a piece for a large ensemble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes M and I out of CHOIRMASTER; 'composed' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large ensemble of instrumental musicians playing together.

clue.text: Prevention of a second execution?

parts.note: topping is British slang for killing, especially by hanging

explanation.surface: A question about whether a reprieve stops someone being hanged a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopping something is preventing it from happening or continuing, the noun sense.

clue.text: Area obstructed, we hear, in queen's city

indicators.note: we hear says the word for obstructed is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: being obstructed means being held up, delayed

explanation.surface: Traffic in a district is held up, reportedly, somewhere in the queen's city.
explanation.walkthrough: The city in South Australia was named after Queen Adelaide, wife of William IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the Australian city named in honour of the consort of King William IV.

clue.text: Dancing attendance after company contracts linked together?

indicators.note: after puts the shortened firm in front, since the reshuffled word comes after it

parts.note: the word company shortens to CO

indicators.note: dancing means the letters of the next word move about

explanation.surface: Staff dance attendance on executives after the firm's contracts are bundled together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing attendance' sounds like fawning service, but 'Dancing' is the anagram signal; 'contracts' says company is abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Concatenated means joined in a series or chain, one thing linked to the next.

clue.text: Insect, caught by eg Darwin, without wings

indicators.note: caught by says the trimmed name sits inside the two-letter abbreviation
losing its wings means the name loses its outermost letters on both sides

explanation.surface: A specimen bug collected by a naturalist such as Darwin, missing its wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eg' is not an example marker here but two letters; 'without wings' strips Darwin's outer letters, and 'caught by' places the remainder inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: The earwig is a common insect with pincers at the rear of its body.

clue.text: Good man with WW soldier cut down behind lines

parts.note: a saint, ST, is a good man

indicators.note: cut down behind means the soldier's word is shortened at its tail end

parts.note: an Anzac was a soldier of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps in the World Wars

explanation.surface: A good man and a wartime soldier are killed behind enemy lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down behind' drops the last letter C from ANZAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines of verse forming a unit of a poem.

clue.text: Carry on with pretence in court

parts.note: an act is a pretence, as in 'it's all an act'
up means appearing in court, as in 'up before the magistrate'

explanation.surface: Someone keeps up a sham during a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave, and carry on is a British idiom for making a fuss or misbehaving.

clue.text: Bishop's saga involving saint a gem

indicators.note: involving means the long story wraps around the saint's letter

parts.note: a saga is a long story, an epic
an opal is a gem

explanation.surface: A bishop's long tale features a saint and a precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopal means relating to bishops or governed by them, so it works as the possessive.

clue.text: Inspire learner to leave my unhappy profession

indicators.note: to leave says the learner's letter departs from the phrase

parts.note: professing or declaring one is unhappy means saying I'm blue
L is the abbreviation for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A trainee is urged to quit a profession they find miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'profession' means a declaration, not a job: the declaration of unhappiness is I'M BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to fill or permeate someone with a feeling or idea, much as inspiring them does.

clue.text: Head on fly? It turns easily

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: to fly is to wing one's way
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: An insect lands on someone's head, which spins round easily.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing nut has two flat projections so it can be screwed on and off by hand without a spanner.

clue.text: Painter, a capital and fashionable one

parts.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: An artist is described as one living in a capital city and a stylish one too.
explanation.definitionFit: Gian Lorenzo Bernini was a Baroque sculptor and architect who also painted.

clue.text: Engineer grapples with a process finally making it smoother

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rearrange, so the letters are reworked
finally picks the closing letter of the word process

explanation.surface: An engineer struggles with a procedure that finally makes things run more smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' rearranges GRAPPLES, A and S, the last of 'process'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasspaper is an abrasive sheet, like sandpaper, rubbed on wood to make a surface smooth.

clue.text: Fever that is rough? Not very

parts.note: a rough estimate is a vague one
